registry.doc: parse(text) -> Result<value>: read JSON with exact signed/unsigned integers in range and document-position refusals
stringify(value) -> Result<String>: render JSON with cycle and depth guards; refuse unrepresentable values
stdin() -> Result<String>: the whole of standard input as UTF-8, up to 8 MiB; Err on a terminal or a second read; not notebook input_request
eprint(text) -> Result<()>: write text to standard error, adding nothing, then flush
Dense: a finite f32/f64 row-major matrix with named columns, at most 2^24 values; adapters exchange numbers through it
shape() -> (rows, columns)
names() -> Vec<String>: the column names
dtype() -> String: "f32" or "f64"

exit(code) -> Result<()>: end the script with this status, which must be 0 to 255; a status outside that ends the script with 1 rather than being truncated; in run or eval it never returns, and in a session or worker it is refused with Err

run(program, args, options) -> Result<#{code, stdout, stderr, timed_out, cancelled, truncated, cut_short, unreadable}>: synchronous supervised child; run returns strict UTF-8 stdout/stderr, run_bytes returns Bytes; options: timeout_ms (default 30000, 1..=90000), input (String or Bytes), cwd, env (String values set, None removes), env_clear (default false). Explicit relative program paths always resolve against rnx's directory, even without cwd; bare names use platform lookup, whose PATH-override behaviour is platform-specific. The deadline starts after spawn. Check timed_out/cancelled before code, then truncated/cut_short/unreadable before trusting capture completeness. Killed children have no code on Unix and code 1 on Windows. Nonzero exit is Ok; launch/validation failures are Err. Input delivery does not certify consumption. No global environment or directory changes.

run_bytes(program, args, options) -> Result<#{code, stdout, stderr, timed_out, cancelled, truncated, cut_short, unreadable}>: synchronous supervised child; run returns strict UTF-8 stdout/stderr, run_bytes returns Bytes; options: timeout_ms (default 30000, 1..=90000), input (String or Bytes), cwd, env (String values set, None removes), env_clear (default false). Explicit relative program paths always resolve against rnx's directory, even without cwd; bare names use platform lookup, whose PATH-override behaviour is platform-specific. The deadline starts after spawn. Check timed_out/cancelled before code, then truncated/cut_short/unreadable before trusting capture completeness. Killed children have no code on Unix and code 1 on Windows. Nonzero exit is Ok; launch/validation failures are Err. Input delivery does not certify consumption. No global environment or directory changes.
escape_html(text) -> String: HTML text/quoted-attribute escaping; &, <, >, quotes escaped again; not JS/CSS/URL validation; input/output <=1 MiB; overflow raises a VM error; borrowed
decode_component(text) -> Result<String>: one percent decode, + literal, malformed % literal, invalid UTF-8 refused; input <=1 MiB; do not decode route params twice; borrowed

parse_form(String|Bytes) -> Result<Object>: URL-encoded form, + is space, first duplicate wins; empty pairs/names retained; invalid UTF-8 refused including duplicates; <=1 MiB, <=1024 raw pairs; borrowed

response(status, String|Bytes body, content_type, headers) -> Result<Object>: canonical response; scalar/vector String|Bytes headers; empty vectors accepted; lowercase names, duplicates/reserved names refused; 200..599; 204/304 empty; body <=1 MiB; <=64 names/values and 16 KiB headers; all inputs borrowed, output independent
html(status, String|Bytes body) -> Result<Object>: response with text/html; charset=utf-8, no extra headers; body not escaped; response limits; borrowed
text(status, String|Bytes body) -> Result<Object>: response with text/plain; charset=utf-8, no extra headers; response limits; borrowed
read(path) -> Result<String>: a regular file as UTF-8, up to 8 MiB; use read_bytes for other bytes
read_bytes(path) -> Result<Bytes>: a regular file's bytes, up to 8 MiB
write_new(path, data) -> Result<()>: write String or Bytes, refusing to overwrite an existing file atomically
write(path, data) -> Result<()>: create or truncate in place and write String or Bytes
append(path, data) -> Result<()>: create or append String or Bytes
exists(path) -> Result<bool>: false for missing or dangling; errors remain errors
metadata(path) -> Result<object>: kind, size, modified_ms since epoch, readonly, symlink; follows the target
read_dir(path) -> Result<Vec<String>>: Unicode entry names, byte-sorted, up to 100000
absolute(path) -> Result<String>: canonicalize an existing path
cwd() -> Result<String>: the working directory, without lossy conversion
temp_dir() -> Result<String>: the temporary directory, without lossy conversion
mkdir(path) -> Result<()>: create one directory
mkdir_all(path) -> Result<()>: create all missing parent directories
copy(from, to) -> Result<()>: copy bytes and permissions to an exclusively created file; failure can leave a partial destination
rename(from, to) -> Result<()>: atomically rename without replacing a destination; no fallback
remove_file(path) -> Result<()>: remove a file or a symlink, not its target
remove_dir(path) -> Result<()>: remove an empty directory
remove_dir_all(path) -> Result<()>: remove a tree without following symlinks; refuse root, cwd and ancestors
join(base, part) -> String: lexical join; an absolute part replaces the base; Windows verbatim bases normalize . and .. for nonempty parts
parent(p) -> Option<String>: lexical parent; parent("a") is Some(""), parent("") is None
file_name(p) -> Option<String>: final name, ignoring trailing separators; .. has no name
file_stem(p) -> Option<String>: name without its last extension; a leading dot alone is not an extension
extension(p) -> Option<String>: last extension, without its dot; a trailing dot gives Some("")
with_extension(p, ext) -> Result<String>: replace the last extension; empty removes only the last; separators in ext are refused
is_absolute(p) -> bool: the running platform's rules; Windows requires a prefix and a root
separator() -> String: the running platform's main path separator
now_ms() -> i64: wall-clock milliseconds since Unix epoch, floored; not an elapsed-time clock
monotonic_ms() -> i64: milliseconds since first call in this process; never decreases; not an epoch timestamp
format(ms, pattern, zone) -> Result<String>: Jiff strftime dialect; fallible, precision chosen by the pattern
rfc3339(ms, zone) -> Result<String>: three fractional digits; refuses negative years and offsets outside whole minutes in ±23:59
parse(text) -> Result<i64>: floor milliseconds; offset or Z required; leap seconds refused, zone annotations checked (Z preserves the instant)
parts(ms, zone) -> Result<Object>: calendar fields, ISO weekday, offset_seconds and resolved zone
from_parts(object, zone) -> Result<i64>: year/month/day required; clock fields default to zero; gaps refused, folds require a valid offset_seconds; weekday and zone fields are informational
sleep(ms).await -> Result<()>: 0..68719476735 ms; inert until awaited, interruptible while pending
find(haystack, needle) -> Option<int>: the byte index of the first occurrence, or None
split_max(text, count) -> Result<Vec<String>>: split on whitespace into at most count fields, the last keeping the rest verbatim; Err on a negative count
group_digits(value) -> String: an integer with a comma every three digits
get(url).await -> Result<object>: bounded HTTP GET
get_bytes(url).await -> Result<object>: bounded HTTP GET
request(method, url, options).await -> Result<object>: bounded HTTP request
request_bytes(method, url, options).await -> Result<object>: bounded HTTP request
args() -> Vec<String>: independent copies of the script's arguments; empty in eval and the session
var(name) -> Result<Option<String>>: missing is None, empty is Some(""); invalid names and non-Unicode values are refused
vars() -> Result<Object>: the environment, first duplicate retained; any non-Unicode entry refuses the whole value
home_dir() -> Result<Option<String>>: the platform's home directory; account/profile fallback can block, non-Unicode paths are refused
